about.title: Susanville Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Susanville's economy runs on a mix of state employment, ranching, forestry, and small local businesses, and each of those jobs comes with its own set of hazards — heavy equipment, vehicles on Rt 36 and Main Street, ladders, machinery, and long shifts. When a work injury happens, California law generally routes the claim through workers' compensation, which pays regardless of fault but limits what you can recover. In some situations, though, a third party outside your employer — a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver — bears responsibility, and that opens the door to a separate injury claim. Sorting out whether your case involves a third party isn't something you should have to figure out alone while recovering. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a fee; we simply connect injured workers in Susanville with an independent attorney who can review the details and explain your options plainly, without pressure or promises about outcomes.

whyChoose.title: Why Susanville Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Third-Party Distinction
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker contributed to your injury, a separate claim may be possible. An independent attorney can help identify whether that applies to your situation.

items.title: We Know the Reporting Clock Matters
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your options. Getting connected with an attorney early helps make sure nothing slips past a deadline.

items.title: We Take Retaliation Concerns Seriously
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim. An attorney in our network can talk through those protections so you're not left guessing about your rights.

items.question: I was hurt on the job in Susanville — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the exclusive path against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. But if a third party outside your employer — like another driver, a subcontractor, or an equipment maker — contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim. An independent attorney can look at the facts and tell you which paths apply.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim if a third party was involved?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. That's separate from the shorter window for reporting to your employer for workers' comp purposes. Because these timelines don't always overlap the way people expect, it helps to get guidance sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does Susanville's small size affect how workplace injury claims are handled?
items.answer: Susanville's job base leans on state work, ranching, forestry, and local businesses, and with corridors like Main Street and Skyline Road seeing regular collisions, on-the-job vehicle injuries do happen here too. The size of the city doesn't change California's underlying law, but local attorneys familiar with Lassen County can be useful for coordinating with nearby employers and insurers.

items.question: Can my employer retaliate against me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or pursue a workers' comp or third-party claim. If you believe that's happened, it's worth discussing with an attorney as part of your overall case.
